To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incidence of CL related microbial keratits is low, that overnight wear and poor hand hygiene practices are the most important risk factors and that overnight wear of silicone hydrogel contact lenses is associated with a higher incidence of CL related keratits than overnight wear of hydrogel contact lenses.
overnight wear of silicone hydrogel CLs and poor hygiene practices are the two most important risk factors for CL related microbial keratitits.
overnight wear of hydrogel and extended wear of silicone hydrogel contact lenses are risk factors for CL related microbial keratits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of evidence-based guidelines for the prevention of microbial keratitis in contact lens wearers.
the dissemination of evidence based guidelines to the membership of a contact lens association.
the development and evaluation of evidence-based guidelines on contact lens-related microbial keratitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BCLA guidelines on CL related microbial are evidence based, but there are some areas of disagreement between the guidelines and practitioner opinion.
there was no change in knowledge or awareness of CL related microbial keratits following dissemination of guidelines to BCLA members.
the BCLA membership is well informed and has a high awareness of the importance of risk factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the guidelines have been accepted by the BCLA membership.
the BCLA is disseminating research evidence and that the membership is responding to the new information.
practitioners are generally aware of the key risk factors and are making appropriate recommendations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BCLA should continue to disseminate research findings to members.
the dissemination of evidence based information can be done via the web, and that the information provided is generally well received by the BCLA membership.
there are still some gaps in the evidence base that require further investigation.
